messages:
maria: heads up — after the driver roll (v2.14) we saw a regression on long sequences tied to KV cache misses. 99p token latency spiked and throughput dropped on our 8k tests. repro trace: trace_id=trc_9f3a

kevin: can you paste a couple of logs? curious if it's a key mismatch or tombstone sweep hitting frequently

maria: logs from runtime (snip):
```
[2026-03-17T18:02:11Z] KVCache: lookup - key=kv://model-X/arch_a/seqbin_8k/ptr:abcd1234 -> MISS (tombstone=true)
[2026-03-17T18:02:11Z] KernelSelector: pick=cuASync_v3 arch_hint=arch_a seqlen_bucket=8192
[2026-03-17T18:02:11Z] KVCache: insert - key=kv://model-X/arch_a_v2/seqbin_8k/ptr:efgh5678 -> OK
```

maria: note the key namespace changed mid-roll (arch_a -> arch_a_v2). seems driver started adding per-kernel salt to key after autotuner change.

aj: ack. this explains it — old keys not being recognized, tombstones appear, and cache warms slowly. any perf numbers?

sara: quick numbers from canary vs baseline (p95 token latency):
- baseline (driver v2.13): p95=220ms, p99=310ms, throughput=12.1k toks/s
- canary (driver v2.14): p95=285ms, p99=420ms, throughput=9.4k toks/s
regression concentrated on seq > 2k. small sequences unaffected.

kevin: root cause likely key schema change from our kernel-aware salt. autotune now encodes kernel signature into key (to avoid cross-kernel pollution) but we didn't include a backwards compat layer. result: double population and extra GC/tombstone checks.

kevin: quick options:
1) driver-side compatibility mapping: for 24-48h translate old_ns -> new_ns on lookup (fast mitigation)
2) runtime accepts both key schemas (cost: extra lookup)
3) migrate keys with a rehash sweep (expensive, needs throttling)

maria: option 1 seems fastest. what's the exact admin call?

aj: admin endpoint we have in staging, example:
```
curl -XPOST "https://admin.internal/cache/alias" \\
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN" \\
  -d '{"from":"kv://model-X/arch_a/","to":"kv://model-X/arch_a_v2/","ttl":86400}'
```
This creates a transient alias so lookups check both namespaces. low-risk.

kevin: also need to fix persistence behavior: when runtime restarts it should persist the active key_schema version and not flip to default. currently driver rollout toggles salt generation on the fly. we need a handshake in the driver<->runtime protocol that includes key_schema_version and kernel_signature_map.

maria: proposal for handshake message (proto-ish):
```
DriverHello {
  key_schema: "kv-schema-v2",
  kernel_signatures: ["cuASync_v3#sha1:abcd","cuSync_v2#sha1:1234"],
  seqlen_profile: "auto-buckets-v1"
}
RuntimeAck {
  accepted_schema: "kv-schema-v2",
  active_kernels: ["cuASync_v3"],
  fallback_keys: ["kv-schema-v1"]
}
```
If RuntimeAck returns fallback_keys, driver can enable aliasing automatically.

sara: important note: rehash sweep will spike disk IO and cause page faults on the pod. if we schedule sweep during off-peak we should also throttle to 5k rehashes/s.

aj: agreed. short-term: roll alias for 48h, enable runtime dual-lookup for canary pods. medium: implement handshake + persistent key_schema on runtime across restarts. long: add migration job with throttled rehash and progress metrics.

kevin: added a small perf test plan in the thread:
- Canary A: alias only (driver alias) -> measure p95/p99, miss rate drop
- Canary B: dual-lookup runtime + alias -> expect faster warm, some extra CPU cost
- Canary C: rehash migrate + remove alias -> best steady-state but heavy IO during run

maria: owners: aj -> rollout alias (now), kevin -> runtime dual-lookup patch (PR target EOD), sara -> schedule rehash job and IO limits (tomorrow), i'll monitor traces and rollback criteria.

devops-bot: deploy: canary-group-3 started for driver v2.14 at 2026-03-17T18:10:00Z :rocket:

maria: thanks. I'll post a short runbook for on-call with rollback command if p99 increases >20% over baseline.

aj: rollback command (internal):
```
POST /admin/driver/rollback
body: {"version":"v2.13", "reason":"kv-cache-regression"}
```

kevin: follow-up note: when we implement key_schema versioning, prefer semantic versions (v1, v2) not timestamp salts — easier to reason about in rollouts. also add a metric kv_key_schema_conflicts to surface cross-schema hits.

maria: +1. closing loop here — will update infra runbook and ping when alias is live. :thumbsup:
